metadata.title: Stage Runner: Every Feature, Played
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-waikthrough walker film. Every gameplay beat is an exact-frame window of a scripted-input take of the real game; no human playtest. Game audio was not captured; narration only. No paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: a game design document in, a playable Godot project out. The prompt is a reconstruction. This game was a two-stage Unity shooter, rebuilt in Godot and finished with a third.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a vertical shooter — fly a wisp up three ruined city streets, shoot the monster army marching down at you, and defeat the Cerberus at the city gate — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 3 stages, 13 monster types and a boss, 14 scripts.
Played here: 3 scripted-input takes, 62 of 62 assertions passing.

beats.narration_text: Stage Runner is a vertical shooter: three streets, a monster army, a boss at the gate. Every feature here is played through real key, mouse and gamepad input, by a script. Nobody has played it by hand yet.

props.text:
Stage Runner
is a twin-stick shooter.
Three streets and a boss.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Every implemented feature but six was played through real input, and sixty-two assertions pass. One defect: R on the pause menu logs a script error, though the restart works. What a script can't tell you is whether stage two is fair, or whether the boss is fun. That's a person's call.

artifactLines: Observed: menus → 3 stages → boss → credits; and contact → game over → retry.
Checks: 62 of 62 film-capture assertions pass; the game's own playtest passes.
Defect: R on the pause menu logs a SCRIPT ERROR (game.gd:606).
Untested: a human playtest, Windows, fullscreen, game audio.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude in your own Godot project: Use Walker on my Godot game. Write an input-only capture script that plays one feature through real key and mouse events, asserts what should happen on screen, and fails loudly if it doesn't. Then tell me one thing the capture can't prove. That last part matters: a script that wins is not a player who had fun. Liam, in for Bear.
